_comment_env: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL deliberately does NOT live here. A settings-file env entry wins over the process environment and over --settings, which made the Aperture gate unoverridable and silently disabled Remote Control (it requires api.anthropic.com). It is now injected as a wrapper default in home/claude.nix, so every invocation still gets the gate but a caller can override it. Telemetry (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY) was enabled here briefly and removed again: with no OTLP collector in the fleet it exported nothing.
_comment_permissions_ccr: The Claude Code Remote (bridge) MCP tools are allowed for the READ-ONLY half only — get_session/list_* answer 'which session am I, what model is serving it, what else is running' without a prompt. Everything that mutates (create_session, archive/unarchive, interrupt, set_title/set_tags, send_later, create/update/delete/fire_trigger, subscribe_pr_activity, add_repo) is deliberately left prompting: those spawn containers, wake siblings or post to GitHub. Listed under BOTH name forms for the reason spelled out in .claude/settings.json's _comment_mcp_names — a claude.ai connector attaches either as 'claude.ai Claude Code Remote' (mcp__claude_ai_Claude_Code_Remote__*) or bare (mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__*), and only the bare form has been observed since 2026-07-28, so pinning one form silently stops matching if that flips back.

permissions._comment_deny: Global token-saving Read denials (home-manager managed via nic-os/home/dotfiles/claude-settings.json, wired to ~/.claude/settings.json in home/claude.nix). permissions.deny Read() rules are Claude Code's real file-exclusion mechanism — .claudeignore is NOT a native feature. Rules follow gitignore semantics and apply to Read/Grep/Glob plus cat/head/tail/sed in Bash, across every project (user-level settings = global). Unanchored patterns (no // or ~ prefix) match at any depth. Conservative: dependencies, lockfiles, build output, minified/maps, caches, logs, binaries/media, and secrets only — never real source code. Secrets entries (*.enc/*.pem/*.key/*.p12) also cover sops-encrypted Trusk deployment/configurations/<env>/secrets/ payloads. Edit to extend; deny merges across scopes and a deny at any level wins.
permissions._comment_transcripts: additionalDirectories scopes reading session transcripts (~/.claude*/projects/**/*.jsonl) so `resume session <id>` and self-inspection do not prompt. Read(*)/Bash(*) were already allowed — the prompt came from the WORKSPACE BOUNDARY: transcripts live outside the project cwd, and only additionalDirectories widens that. Scoped to projects/ deliberately, NOT the whole ~/.claude: the parent holds .credentials.json.

_comment_denied_mcp: DEDUPLICATION, not removal — deliberately asymmetric, unlike .claude/settings.json where each connector is listed under BOTH name forms to drop it entirely. Gmail attaches TWICE per session: observed 2026-08-25 in bridge session ancc_9c9e0e76218174a1 as mcp__Gmail__* AND mcp__claude_ai_Gmail__*, the same 28 tools, the combined MCP group costing 37,178 tokens. The two registrations are attempted independently and matched by raw === on the registration name (no trim, no case fold, no 'claude.ai ' strip), and the name space is closed at two forms — so denying exactly one form leaves exactly one attachment. Denying the bare 'Gmail' is what keeps 'claude.ai Gmail', which is also the only form this file's permissions.allow lists (mcp__claude_ai_Gmail). Do NOT add 'claude.ai Gmail' here: that drops Gmail outright. Deliberately USER scope rather than nic-os project scope — a duplicate is pure waste in every repo, while Gmail itself is real work in the Trusk ones. CAVEAT, unverified: 'claude.ai Metabase Trusk' has been denied under both forms since 2f8d755 (2026-08-18) and still attached on 08-19 and again on 08-25, so this mechanism has no positive evidence of biting for claude.ai connectors. Confirm with the mcp_instructions_delta/deferred_tools_delta addedNames recipe in known_issue_claude_connector_deny_both_name_forms before counting the saving.
_comment_pg_rw: Write-capable Trusk monodb MCPs (defined in home/mcp.nix): postgres_staging_rw and postgres_prod_rw both attach normally and are gated per-call by permissions.ask — not denied. The ask gate DOES survive --dangerously-skip-permissions (measured 2026-09-03 in `claude -p` sessions: postgres_prod_ro, not in ask, ran unprompted; staging_rw, in ask, was blocked with 'needs your approval' under the same flag, and an ask-less --settings override did not help since ask merges across scopes and any scope's rule applies). Consequence: rw calls are unusable in ANY non-interactive session (-p, cron, bridge) because there is nobody to answer the prompt — that is the intended safety property, not a bug. Use rw from an interactive session and approve the prompt; for scripted writes, drive the wrapper in home/mcp.nix directly over MCP stdio.
